say: Get through lane on last hits, then hunt their carries once you have your ultimate, or push a side lane if they're grouped too tight.
more: Akali is weak while she has one dash and a small energy bar. The game opens up when Perfect Execution gives her two more leaps to reach a back line and get out again.
Twilight Shroud is what keeps you alive in both halves: it hides you and makes you untargetable to their spells and attacks, as long as you stop attacking for a moment.
If their team stands together with stuns ready, a side lane pulls one of them away, and a lone opponent is exactly what Akali wants to meet.
check: Whether their carries are standing alone or wrapped in crowd control, and how much energy you have before you jump.
breaks: If they have several point-and-click stuns or reveals, diving first gets you killed; enter after those are used, or stay on the side lane and make them come to you.

when: you are level 6, or level 5 and close to it
asks: can I kill them at six
when do I go in on Akali
say: Level six gives you Perfect Execution, so all-in a laner who's already chipped down, or take it to a side lane if yours is healthy.
more: The second cast of Perfect Execution hits harder the lower they are, so the kill comes from chipping first and using the recast last, not from opening with everything.
A roam with your ultimate up is strong because side laners have no idea a second dash is coming. A kill there also gets you gold without your own laner needing to make a mistake.
Your first finished damage item is the second jump in power. After it, one full rotation threatens squishy champions from most of their health.
check: Your laner's health and whether they still have an escape or a stun to stop your second dash.
breaks: If your laner is healthy and has their stun ready, the all-in fails; push the wave first and look sideways instead, or keep farming until they're low.

asks: how do I trade on Akali
how do I win lane as Akali
what's the Akali combo in lane
how do I poke as Akali
say: Hit Five Point Strike, step out of the ring, then land the long empowered attack; or drop Twilight Shroud and just farm if they out-range you.
more: Assassin's Mark is the whole trade pattern: spell damage makes the ring, leaving it gives your next attack extra range and damage. Walking away from them is how you set up the hit.
Everything costs energy, so two or three spells and you're empty. Trade in short bursts, then last-hit while it comes back.
Shuriken Flip marks them for a dash, but using it leaves you with no way out. Throw it when their jungler has shown elsewhere.
check: Your energy bar, where their jungler was last seen, and whether your flip is available as an escape.
breaks: If you're taking more than you deal, stop trading; use the shroud only to last-hit safely and wait for level six.

when: your lane opponent is a ranged champion
asks: how do I lane against ranged as Akali
I'm getting poked out on Akali
Akali into a mage what do I do
they just auto me every time I farm
say: Give up a few minions early and save Twilight Shroud for when they walk up to trade, or look for a Shuriken Flip all-in at six.
more: Ranged champions win the first levels against you by hitting you every time you last-hit. Losing a little farm costs less than losing half your health and the wave with it.
The shroud stops them targeting you, so a trade they start often ends with them standing too far forward. That's your window to hit back.
At six the lane flips: one landed shuriken gives you three dashes onto someone with no front line.
check: How far forward the wave is and whether they've just used their main spell on the minions.
breaks: If the wave is frozen on their side and you can't reach it, don't walk into it; ask for a gank or roam, since standing there only loses health.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Akali
who do I go on as Akali
when do I jump in on Akali
say: Wait for their stuns to be used, then dive the back line with your ultimate; or come in from the side later to finish low targets.
more: Going in first makes you the target for everything. Going in second, when their crowd control is spent on your front line, lets the shroud and your dashes actually keep you alive.
The recast of your ultimate is an execute, so it's often right to hold the second dash for the moment someone drops low, or as your way out.
If their carries are protected too well, killing whoever is closest and low is still worth more than waiting forever for the perfect target.
check: Which of their stuns and reveals have been used, and where their carries are standing.
breaks: If they keep everything for you and never spend it, don't force it; split a side lane so someone has to leave the group to answer you.

say: You're a pick champion: threaten Rocket Grab from brush so they play scared, or run at them with Overdrive and Power Fist once the grab's used.
more: The grab is worth more as a threat than as a spell. While you hold it, their bot lane has to stand behind minions and gives up farm and position.
One grab on a carry before an objective turns the fight into five against four. That's how Blitzcrank wins games from even or behind.
A missed grab leaves you with very little for a while, so their lane will step forward the moment it's gone.
check: Whether there's a clear line to the target with no minion in the way, and whether your carry is close enough to follow.
breaks: If they have a tank who wants to be pulled in, grabbing does their engage for them; play as a bodyguard with Power Fist instead.

asks: when can we fight bot as Blitz
is level two good on Blitz
say: Level two with grab and Power Fist is your first kill window, or wait for six when Static Field's silence finishes the job.
more: Getting level two before their lane means a grab into a knock-up while they're missing an ability. Pushing the first wave with your carry sets that up.
Static Field removes shields and silences briefly, so at six a grabbed target can't flash-spell their way out or be saved by a shield as easily.
Later your power is just the grab itself. It doesn't need items, which is why Blitzcrank stays dangerous even when behind.
check: Which lane is going to hit level two first, and whether your carry has the damage to finish a grabbed target.
breaks: If their lane out-pushes you early, you won't get level two first; hold the grab as a threat near your tower rather than forcing it.

asks: how do I lane as Blitz
when should I throw the grab
say: Stand to the side of their minions so the grab has a path, and throw after they dash; or zone by walking up without casting.
more: Minions block the grab, so your position matters more than your aim. Standing in the side brush or level with their caster minions opens the angle.
Most people dodge sideways when you walk at them. Waiting until they've used a dash, or are mid-animation on a last hit, makes it far easier.
Walking forward with the grab held makes them back off the wave. That pressure costs them farm and costs you nothing.
check: Where the minions are between you and the target, and whether their escape spell has been used.
breaks: If you miss, back off straight away; they know you have nothing and will trade onto you or your carry until it's back.

when: your bot laner is dead or has recalled
asks: my adc backed what do I do
can I go mid as Blitzcrank
where do I go while my carry's gone
say: Overdrive makes your roam quick, so walk mid for a grab while your carry's away, or sit in river brush and guard the wave's return.
more: A two-person lane with one person is just a place to die. Mid is the shortest walk, and a grab from the side brush there is very hard to see coming.
Even a missed grab mid forces a flash or pushes their laner off the wave, which gives your mid the push and first move to the next river fight.
Time it so you're back bot when your carry arrives. A long roam that leaves them alone against two costs more than the roam earned.
check: Whether mid's wave is pushed toward your side, so their laner is far from their tower, and how long until your carry is back.
breaks: If the bot wave is about to crash into your tower, stay and hold it from a safe distance instead; lost minions and plates outweigh a maybe-grab.

asks: what do I do in fights as Blitz
who do I hook in teamfights
say: The grab is for a pick before the fight: pull someone out of position, or stay beside your carry and Power Fist whoever dives.
more: Once a fight is already going, pulling an enemy into your team can deliver their tank exactly where it wanted to be. Before the fight, the same grab wins it outright.
Static Field's silence is best on a cluster as they commit, or on a mage about to cast. It also strips shields, which matters against enchanters.
If nothing is grabbable, your knock-up and silence make you a good bodyguard. Peeling one diver off your carry is a full job.
check: Who is standing at the edge of their group, and whether your team is close enough to kill what you pull.
breaks: If your team is too far back to follow, don't grab; a pulled target who lives just walks away with your main spell used.

when: their support is a melee engage tank
asks: what do I do against a tank support as Blitz
say: Don't pull their engage tank onto your carry; aim grabs at their marksman, or hold Power Fist to knock up the tank when it jumps.
more: Grabbing a champion who wants to be in melee range saves them the hard part of their job. The marksman behind them is the only target worth the spell.
Against engage, your knock-up and silence are an answer: interrupting the tank right as it lands gives your carry the second it needs to walk away.
This usually means a slower lane. That's fine; your grab keeps its value all game while their early engage window closes.
check: Whether the tank is standing in front of their marksman and blocking the line.
breaks: If their marksman steps out alone past the tank, take the grab; if never, play to counter-engage and wait for mid-game picks.

asks: what does Elise want to do
say: You're an early-game jungler: gank with Cocoon before lanes get their items and snowball them, or invade their jungler if nothing's gankable.
more: Elise brings a stun, a gap closer and burst very early, at a point when laners are still weak. That's the window she's picked for.
She doesn't out-scale farming junglers, so a quiet first ten minutes is a loss for you even if your farm looks fine.
The lead you build should go into lanes and objectives, because later you're a pick champion who needs teammates strong enough to finish fights.
check: Which enemy laners are pushed forward without an escape, and where their jungler started.
breaks: If every lane is pushed under their own tower, ganks won't work; take their camps or set up the first dragon with your stronger early fighting.

when: before 4:00
asks: how do I clear on Elise
full clear or gank on Elise
say: Open each camp in human form, finish in spider form to heal, then gank after three camps; or full clear if no lane's pushed up.
more: Neurotoxin hits harder on a full-health monster and Venomous Bite harder on a low one, so human first, spider second gets the most from both.
Spider form attacks restore health and your spiderlings help with the camp, which is what keeps you healthy enough to gank straight from the clear.
Elise prefers ganking to farming. Three camps toward the lane you want to visit gets you there before most junglers finish a full clear around level four.
check: Your health after the buff, and which lane is pushed toward your side as you finish the third camp.
breaks: If lanes are even or pushing your way, don't force it; finish the clear and be at a river crab when they spawn at 2:55.

asks: who do I gank as Elise
which lane should I gank on Elise
how do I gank on Elise
where do I go as Elise
say: Gank the lane whose opponent has no dash, since everything rides on Cocoon landing; or come from behind so they must walk toward you.
more: Cocoon is a narrow skill shot that stops on the first unit it hits. Minions block it, so the angle you arrive from matters as much as the target.
A lane with its own crowd control makes your stun easy: their slow or root lands first and you can't miss a still target.
After the stun, switch to spider and use Venomous Bite late in the combo, because it deals more the lower they are.
check: Whether minions are between you and the target, and whether that laner has used their escape recently.
breaks: If the Cocoon misses, don't chase far; you've shown yourself, so take the nearby camp or crab and try another lane.

when: an enemy laner is at least one level behind your laner
say: With a big wave under their tower, stun, burst, and Rappel up as the tower turns on you; or wait and take plates if they're healthy.
more: Rappel lifts Elise off the ground for a moment and brings her down on a target. Used mid-dive it buys time while your laner takes the tower's attention or the kill finishes.
Dives work on a level or health lead plus a stacked wave. The wave soaks tower shots and denies them farm and experience when they die.
A successful dive on a side lane often decides it for good: the laner comes back to a lost wave and a tower already chipped.
check: The enemy laner's health, the size of your wave, and whether their jungler could be nearby.
breaks: If their jungler hasn't shown and the wave is small, skip it; a failed dive hands over two kills and your early window.

asks: how long do I have to snowball
say: Your strongest window is early, while laners are still low level, so force plays now, or trade camps for a dragon if ganks are covered.
more: Elise's damage doesn't depend on a big item. It's there from the first few levels, which is why her kills come early and thin out later.
Each successful gank should turn into something lasting: a tower chipped, a dragon, or their jungle camps. Kills alone fade as the game goes on.
By the time carries finish several items, your burst only kills someone caught alone. Plan for that by getting teammates ahead, not just yourself.
check: The game clock against your kill and assist count; a quiet scoreline at ten minutes means changing the plan.
breaks: If you're already behind, stop forcing ganks into lanes that are losing; farm, hold vision around the next objective and look for a Cocoon pick.

asks: what do I do late as Elise
how do I teamfight as Elise
say: Late, you're a pick champion: land Cocoon on someone walking alone and burst them, or stay by your carry and stun whoever dives.
more: One stun from fog before baron or elder dragon is still game-winning, because a five against four at those objectives usually ends it.
In a full fight you can't dive five people. Using Cocoon to stop their diver and Rappel to dodge their big spell keeps you useful and alive.
Set up in brush on the path they have to take toward the objective. Arriving first is what makes a pick champion work.
check: Which enemy tends to walk alone to side lanes or wards, and whether your team is close enough to follow the pick.
breaks: If they move as five with vision, there's no pick; stay grouped, peel, and let your carries decide the fight.

say: You win by owning ground: set turrets, push the wave, and make them fight inside your nest, or chip their tower if they refuse.
more: Heimerdinger is strong where his turrets already stand and weak everywhere else. Every decision is about getting the fight to happen on your prepared spot.
Constant pushing denies their laner farm under tower and lets you move first, but it also leaves you far forward, so river vision matters more than for most champions.
Turrets deal half damage to towers, so sieging is slow and steady. The real gain is that they can't leave lane without losing the tower.
check: How many turrets you have down and where, and whether you can see the river on the side a gank comes from.
breaks: If they have long range that kills turrets safely, the nest loses; keep turrets further back and farm with rockets instead.

when: you are level 6 or higher
say: At six you can upgrade one spell: the big turret to win an all-in at your nest, or the upgraded grenade to catch or escape.
more: The upgraded turret turns a gank on you into a fight you can win, as long as it happens next to the turrets you already placed.
The upgraded grenade is the catch tool. A direct hit stuns, which sets up your own rockets or a teammate's follow-up.
Upgraded rockets are the burst option on someone already stunned or standing still. Picking the wrong upgrade is the most common way to waste the spike.
check: Whether the threat in front of you is a dive, a chase or a poke war, since each wants a different upgrade.
breaks: If you use the upgrade for wave clear, you have nothing when their jungler arrives; keep it while their jungler is unseen.

asks: how do I trade as Heimer
how do I lane as Heimerdinger
how do I poke on Heimer
say: Keep turrets just behind your minions and trade only inside their range; open with the grenade stun, or rockets alone if they stay back.
more: A turret that the enemy can reach without taking damage is a free kill for them. Behind your wave, they have to walk through minions and beams to get to it.
The grenade only stuns on a direct hit and slows around it. Landing it first makes the rockets converge on a target that can't sidestep.
Turrets do the pushing for you, so spend your own attention on last hits and on watching the river.
check: How many turret charges you're holding and whether the enemy is clearing turrets for free.
breaks: If they destroy turrets from range every time, stop placing them forward; set them near your tower and farm with rockets.

asks: I keep getting ganked on Heimer
how do I not die pushed up
wave's always pushed what do I do
say: Turrets shove the wave regardless, so build the nest beside the brush a gank comes through and fight there, or place one and hold the wave.
more: You can't easily freeze on Heimerdinger, so plan for being pushed. Turrets set toward the river entrance make the gank path the most dangerous place in lane for them.
Hextech Affinity gives you move speed near your turrets and allied towers, which is your escape if you stay inside the nest instead of running through open lane.
Placing fewer turrets slows the push when you need the wave closer to home, for example when their jungler is ahead and unseen.
check: Which river entrance is unwarded, and whether their jungler has shown on the other side of the map.
breaks: If their jungler and laner together can burst you before turrets matter, don't stand and fight; back to your tower early and rebuild there.

asks: what do I do for dragon as Heimer
how do I help with objectives on Heimerdinger
where do I go before dragon
say: Arrive at the pit early and plant turrets in the choke before they come, or shove a side lane hard so they must send someone.
more: Turrets need time to be placed, so a late arrival leaves you with one. Getting there well before the objective spawns turns the entrance into your nest.
A team that has to walk through three turrets and a grenade to contest usually gives the objective or starts the fight already hurt.
If your team can't hold the pit anyway, your push is the trade: you take a tower fast enough that their objective isn't free.
check: How long until the objective spawns and which entrance they're likely to use.
breaks: If they arrive first and hold the choke, don't walk turrets into them; push the far side lane and take a tower for it.

asks: is Karma a poke or shield champ
say: Early you're a lane bully with Mantra Inner Flame; later you shield and speed your team, or keep poking if you built damage.
more: Karma is strongest in the first part of the game, when an empowered Inner Flame takes a real piece of someone's health.
As fights get bigger, Inspire becomes the main button: a shield and a burst of speed decides whether your engager reaches them or your carry gets away.
The plan is to cash the early pressure into towers and dragons before your damage stops mattering.
check: Whether your early poke actually won the lane, which decides if you stay aggressive or become the shield.
breaks: If their lane out-sustains your poke, stop spending mana on it; hold Mantra for shields and play for your jungler.

asks: when do I fight as Karma
say: Mantra works from level one, so your best moment is right now: poke hard early, or keep Mantra for a shield if they threaten a kill.
more: Most champions wait for level six for their ultimate. Karma has hers from the start, which is why she can win the first few levels against almost anyone.
Hitting champions with damaging spells shortens Mantra's cooldown, so landing poke gives you more empowered spells, and missing gives you fewer.
That edge shrinks once others reach six, so the lead has to be built before then.
check: Your mana, since early poke runs it down fast, and whether their jungler could be near while you stand forward.
breaks: If you're low on mana by the time they hit six, the lane flips; recall on a pushed wave before that happens.

asks: how do I trade as Karma
how do I poke on Karma
when do I use Mantra in lane
say: Throw Mantra Inner Flame through gaps in the wave when it's ready, or tether with Focused Resolve and back away until the root lands.
more: Inner Flame explodes on the first enemy it meets, so a clear line or a target standing next to their minions is what you're looking for.
Focused Resolve only roots if the tether holds. Use Inspire's speed on yourself to stay in range while moving away from their damage.
The tether is also your answer to someone jumping on you: they chose to be close, so the root is almost guaranteed.
check: Whether a minion is blocking the line, and how much mana the next rotation costs you.
breaks: If they dodge most of your poke, slow down; an empty mana bar with no damage done leaves you nothing to answer an all-in.

asks: what do I do in fights as Karma
say: Put a Mantra Inspire on whoever is starting the fight or getting dived, or use Mantra Inner Flame to poke before it begins.
more: The speed from Inspire is the real value: it closes the gap for an engage or opens one for an escape. Choose by asking who needs to move right now.
Before an objective, poke is better. A team that arrives at the pit already hurt can't contest.
Stay behind your front line. You do your job from range, and a dead Karma shields nobody.
check: Who your team's engager is, and which carry the enemy is trying to reach.
breaks: If their dive goes straight onto you, shield yourself and tether the diver; your own survival comes first.

asks: what do I do mid game as Karma
how do I use my lead on Karma
say: Your poke matters less every minute, so turn the lead into towers and dragons now, or shift to protecting your best carry.
more: Karma's advantage is tempo: she's strong early and moves fast. Spending that on objectives turns a temporary edge into a permanent one.
Poking a tower's defenders until they have to leave is a clean way to take it without a fight.
If the lead never came, your value is still high as a shield and speed source. The switch in mindset is the important part.
check: Which objective is next and whether your team is strong enough to start it after your poke.
breaks: If your carries are behind, don't siege into a stronger team; stall with wave clear and shields until they catch up.

say: You're a fast-farming jungler who fights on the move: clear quickly and keep your speed stacked, or join fights where the sleep hits several.
more: Blooming Blows gives stacking move speed for landing spells, so Lillia gets safer and stronger the longer a fight lasts, as long as she keeps hitting.
Her passive burns a share of max health over time. That shreds tanks and monsters, and it's why she's good at drawn-out fights around objectives.
Standing still is how Lillia dies. She has no dash, only speed, so fight on the edge and never in the middle.
check: Whether your speed stacks are up before you commit, and whether they have point-and-click crowd control.
breaks: If they have reliable stuns and burst, edge fighting gets you caught; stay behind your front line and use the sleep to defend.

when: before 4:00
asks: how do I clear on Lillia
do I gank early on Lillia
say: Full clear, kiting each camp at the edge of Blooming Blows so you take little damage, or stop early if a lane brings its own stun.
more: The outer edge of Blooming Blows deals extra true damage, and moving between casts means monsters hit you less. Her clear is fast and healthy when kited.
Lillia prefers farming early. A full clear is about level four, and she'd sooner reach six quickly than gamble on a gank with only a slow.
Finishing near a river crab at 2:55 gives you a safe, fast camp and a look at where their jungler is.
check: Your health at the end of the clear and which side of the map their jungler shows on.
breaks: If their jungler is a strong early fighter and invades, don't fight in your own camps; give one and take the opposite side.

when: you are below level 6
asks: who do I gank as Lillia
should I gank or farm on Lillia
say: Before six you only have Swirlseed's slow, so gank lanes that bring their own stun, or keep clearing and meet their jungler at crab.
more: Swirlseed rolls until it hits something, so it can start a gank from a long way off. But a slow alone rarely kills anyone with a flash.
A laner with a root or stun turns your slow into a kill, because your speed lets you stay on the target while the max-health burn ticks.
Otherwise each camp is worth more to you than a low-chance gank. Level six is where your ganks become real.
check: Which of your laners has crowd control, and whether the enemy laner is pushed past the middle of the lane.
breaks: If a lane is overextended and low anyway, go; a slow is enough on someone with half health and a long run home.

when: you are level 6, or level 5 and close to it
asks: what do I do at six on Lillia
how do I use Lillia ult
say: Six is your big jump: tag several people with spells, then put them to sleep for your team, or keep farming if nobody can follow.
more: Lilting Lullaby only affects enemies you've already hit, so the ultimate is the second step. The first is landing spells on as many as possible.
Sleeping targets take extra damage when woken, so the first hit should be a big one. A small poke that wakes them wastes most of it.
The first dragon or grub fight after six is the natural place to use it: enemies bunch up in a tight space.
check: How many enemies are marked before you cast, and whether a teammate is close enough to hit the sleeping target.
breaks: If your team is far away, the sleep just delays them; use it to get out or to stop a chase instead.

asks: what do I do in fights as Lillia
when do I ult on Lillia
who do I hit as Lillia
say: Circle the edge hitting as many as you can, then sleep them; or keep the sleep to stop their dive on your carry.
more: Every spell you land adds speed and starts the max-health burn, so hitting the front line is fine. You're not looking for one target, you're looking for many.
A sleep on three or more is an engage your whole team can walk into. A sleep on their diver is a full stop to their plan.
Stay moving around the outside. Each pass through gives another Blooming Blows and keeps you out of their crowd control.
check: How many of them carry your mark, and where their hard crowd control is pointed.
breaks: If they spread out so you can only tag one or two, don't force the big ultimate; use it on whoever threatens your carry.

say: You're the anti-engage support: keep Black Shield for their crowd control and punish with Dark Binding, or shove the wave with Tormented Shadow.
more: Black Shield blocks disabling effects while it holds. Against teams that need one stun to start a fight, that single spell can cancel their whole plan.
Dark Binding is a long root. Landing it on a carry is a kill for your lane early and a pick for your team later.
Tormented Shadow clears waves well, which gives your lane the push and lets you leave first for wards or a roam.
check: Which enemy crowd control is the one that matters, so you know what the shield is waiting for.
breaks: If they have little crowd control, the shield is only a magic damage block; play more for bindings and wave pressure.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: what do I do at six on Morgana
how do I use Morgana ult
say: Six adds Soul Shackles: walk into them after a binding lands and stay close, or keep it to punish whoever dives your carry.
more: Soul Shackles chains nearby enemy champions and gives you move speed, so it rewards being in the middle and staying there. A root first makes that much easier.
Used defensively, it turns their dive around. The diver is already next to you and now has to leave or stay chained.
Black Shield on yourself before you walk in protects you from the stun that would stop it.
check: Whether a binding has landed or their escape is used, and how much damage they can put on you while you stand in range.
breaks: If they can simply walk or dash out, don't lead with it; hold it as the answer to their engage.

asks: how do I lane as Morgana
when do I throw Q on Morgana
say: Throw Dark Binding as they step up for a last hit or right after their dash, or drop Tormented Shadow on them for safer chip.
more: The binding is slow and blocked by minions, so thrown at random it misses and leaves you with nothing. Tie it to a moment when they can't move freely.
Tormented Shadow under a bound target does much more, since its damage grows as they get lower.
Soul Siphon heals you from damage to champions and large minions, so trading with the pool keeps you healthier than it looks.
check: Whether minions block the line, and whether your binding is the only thing keeping their engage away.
breaks: If their support is waiting for your binding to be used before going in, hold it; the threat is worth more than a low-chance cast.

when: their support is a hook or engage champion
asks: how do I play Morgana into hooks
when do I use Black Shield
who do I shield in lane
say: Stay near your carry and Black Shield them as the hook flies, not before; or shield yourself if you're the one standing in front.
more: The shield has a limited duration, so casting it early lets them wait it out. Casting on reaction to the hook or jump is what cancels it.
Magic damage breaks the shield, so a good opponent will poke it off first. If that happens, step back until it's ready again.
Once their engage has been blocked, they have nothing for a while. That's your moment to walk up and throw the binding.
check: Who their engage is aimed at, and whether the shield is ready before your carry steps forward.
breaks: If the shield is down, tell your carry to give up the wave for a moment; one caught carry costs more than a few minions.

asks: what do I do in fights as Morgana
say: Shield the carry their crowd control is aimed at, then bind the diver; or shield your engager so they can't be stopped going in.
more: A shielded carry can keep attacking through the stun that was meant to kill them. That's often the whole fight.
On an engager, the shield means their dive can't be interrupted. Pick whichever of your teammates is deciding the fight.
Keep the binding for whoever comes to you. A diver rooted next to your carry is a free kill.
check: Which enemy spell starts their fights and who it usually lands on.
breaks: If their threat is physical burst with no crowd control, the shield won't save anyone; stand back and use binding and shackles to peel.

say: You're an anti-dash tank: stand by your carry and stop divers with Steadfast Presence, or hunt wall stuns with Heroic Charge for picks.
more: Steadfast Presence stops enemy dashes around you. Against champions who need to jump onto a carry, standing in the right place shuts them down.
Heroic Charge only stuns when the target hits terrain, so Poppy is far stronger in the jungle and near walls than in the open middle of a lane.
